_comment: NHL 2K10 uniform decal ('stamp') SOURCE cells, plus the one destination rect still in use.
src_cell = rect in the 2048x512 stamps.dds sheet, in PIXELS (x0,y0,x1,y1).
Decoded from the pixel-shader float constants of the player draws:
cN = (slotW, slotH, slotU0, slotV0) and cN+1 = (u0, v0, u1, v1), both
normalised to the 2048x512 sheet. cN is a PADDED slot: the tight glyph rect
cN+1 centred in it (verified exactly, e.g. 0.699707 = 0.70166 - (79-71)/2/2048).
WHY THE dst_cell RECTS ARE GONE
Every stamp except the back NAME is now placed by the game's own shader math
(launcher/stamp_shader.py + data/stamp_shader.json), which has no destination
rectangle at all: the crest rides an affine function of the base UV, and the
numbers and letters ride decal quads baked into the mesh. Both were reproduced
pixel-exactly against the game's own render target.
The rects that used to live here were measured, but a rect blit has to STRETCH
the art to fill its rect, and the measurements were not tight enough to survive
that: the crest rect was 278x277 where the shader's own mask works out to
204x205, a 36% oversize that ran the crest into the jersey's stripes. Keeping
them around would only invite someone to place a new stamp the wrong way, so
only back_name -- which genuinely still needs one -- keeps its rect.
The back NAME is a third mechanism: draw 1055 binds two 1024x256 RGBA8 textures
holding a PRE-RENDERED name strip, positioned by a switch/case affine rather
than by either stamp layer. Until that affine is decoded the nameplate stays on
its measured rect, and stamp_shader.unshaded() reports it as such.
keyed=true means the art is colour-keyed rather than literal: the blue channel is
the fill mask and green/red are outline masks, recoloured from the team palette.
flip180 = the art is rotated 180 degrees before blitting. The shirt is unwrapped
flat across the SHOULDER seam (front panel v 608-1021, back panel v 1-510, arms
between), so back art is stored upside-down.

letter.comment: The captured player wears an 'A'. The 'C' cell is the neighbouring 128px column (896,256)-(1024,512). Placement comes from decal slot 1 of the shirt piece -- see stamp_shader.json.

back_name.measured_from: bake_back_num_1055: 'CELEBRINI' ink bbox x[422,600] y[372,433]; centred on the back-panel axis x=511, cell widened to 300 so longer names still fit
